facts.label: My requests
facts.description: The customer's requests (FDD 7.18.4; wireframe Portal requests; replaces customer-my-requests). Chips by what needs the customer, search, a tracker per row; a row opens its tracking page, a ready quote opens the quote. Data: loadRequestsChain (views/customer-my-requests, as the old list).

fields: Request number, customer, contact or contract

chains.name: customersModuleGuardChain
chains.about: Page guard for the CUSTOMERS_MODULE_ENABLED module licence, from Old EquipRite's customer-portal/pages/*-page-chains/customersModuleGuardChain.js. Every customer page runs it first on vbEnter: with the Customers module off it says so and sends the user home, so a bookmark or deep link cannot open a portal page the menu hides. Same copy in every customer page's chains folder. One change: it waits briefly for the flags to load before deciding. The old copy decided at once and, flags still loading on a cold start, sent a licensed user home; it still fails closed if they never arrive. UX layer…

chains.name: enforcePageAccessChain
chains.about: Page-level RBAC deep-link guard. GENERATED - every copy is byte-identical; change the template and regenerate rather than editing one copy. Copies exist because a page's eventListeners resolve a bare chain id against that page's OWN <page>-chains folder, so an app-level chain referenced by name 404s. This file holds NO policy: the decision (canEnterPage), the page code (getPageCodeForPage), the redirect target (getRoleHomeTarget) and the same-flow test (isSameFlow) all live in $application.functions. Deriving the page code at runtime is what lets every copy be identical.

chains.name: filterChain
chains.about: Chip, search text and "Show more". The filtering itself is customer-requests-page.js filterRows.

chains.name: goChain
chains.about: Opens another customer portal page, with the request when one is given (requestId = number, requestNumericId = id, the old customer pages' parameters). Buttons carry data-page / data-id / data-number. Only the portal's own pages; the billing pages only while EXTERNAL_PROJECT_ASSIGN_ENABLED is off (the old nav's hiddenWhenFlags and navigateToMyBillingChain rule). Same copy in every customer page that links to another.

chains.name: loadRequestsChain
chains.about: The customer's requests: Old EquipRite's customer-my-requests-page-chains/EquipmentRequestInitChain.js, same endpoint and parameters (views/customer-my-requests, page 0, size 200) and the same row mapping. Newest first. The view is scoped to the signed-in customer server-side.

modules.name: customerPortal
modules.about: The customer portal's shared logic (New EquipRite, flows/customer): the words a customer sees for each status, the parcel-style tracker, "what needs you next", and the invoice maths. Pure functions, no calls: the chains read and write through the old endpoints and hand the rows here. The invoice part (parseDate … invoiceTotals) is carried over unchanged from Old EquipRite's flows/customer-portal/pages/customer-billing-detail-page-chains/BillingDetailInitChain.js, so a customer sees the same…

ai.text:
## What this page is for
- The customer-portal list of the signed-in customer's own equipment requests (FDD 7.18.4, wireframe "Portal requests"). It replaces the old `customer-my-requests` page.
- It shows each request with a parcel-style tracker of where it stands, so the customer can see what needs their attention.
- From here the customer can open a request's tracking page, or its quote when one is ready.
- The page is read-only: its only backend call is one GET.

## How people use it
- The single "My requests" section is a table with columns Request, Dates, Where it is, Contract and Actions.
- Chips at the top filter the list by what needs the customer. The exact chip labels are not in the facts.
- A search box ("Search your requests") takes a request number, customer, contact or contract.
- "Show more" reveals more of the list.
- Row actions are **Track** (the tracking page), **Quote** and **Accept quote** (the quote page), plus a generic **Go** button.
- Header actions are **Customer portal** (back to the portal home) and **New request**.

## Business logic
- **Before the page opens:** `enforcePageAccessChain` (vbBeforeEnter) is the role-based deep-link guard.
  - It holds no policy of its own. The decision (`canEnterPage`), page code (`getPageCodeForPage`), redirect target (`getRoleHomeTarget`) and same-flow test (`isSameFlow`) all live in `$application.functions`.
- **On open, licence check:** `customersModuleGuardChain` (vbEnter) checks the `CUSTOMERS_MODULE_ENABLED` module licence.
  - If the module is off, it tells the user and sends them home, so a bookmark or deep link cannot open a page the menu hides.
  - It waits briefly for the feature flags to load before deciding, and fails closed if they never arrive.
- **On open, data load:** `loadRequestsChain` (vbEnter) calls `views/customer-my-requests` with page 0, size 200.
  - It uses the same endpoint, parameters and row mapping as the old `EquipmentRequestInitChain.js`.
  - Rows are sorted newest first.
  - The view is scoped to the signed-in customer on the server.
- **Filtering:** `filterChain` handles chip selection, search input and "Show more" (events onChip, onSearch, onMore).
  - The filtering itself is done by `filterRows` in `customer-requests-page.js`.
  - Only `loadRequestsChain` is listed as calling the REST endpoint, so filtering appears to work on the rows already loaded.
- **Navigation:** `goChain` (onGo) drives every navigation button: Customer portal, New request, Go, Track, Quote and Accept quote.
  - Buttons carry `data-page`, `data-id` and `data-number`.
  - When a request is given, it is passed as `requestId` = the request number and `requestNumericId` = the id (the old customer pages' parameters).
  - It only opens the portal's own pages.
  - Billing pages are reachable only while `EXTERNAL_PROJECT_ASSIGN_ENABLED` is off (the old nav's `hiddenWhenFlags` / `navigateToMyBillingChain` rule).
- **Accept quote:** on this page it only navigates through `goChain`. The acceptance itself is not performed here.
- **Status wording and tracker:** the shared `customerPortal` rules module supplies the customer-facing words for each status, the parcel-style tracker and "what needs you next".
  - These are pure functions with no calls.
  - The module also holds invoice maths, which nothing in this page's facts appears to use.
